registry.toolNetcaptureDesc: Observe a local app's API requests over CDP and turn the one you pick into a site descriptor for Auto Check-in; no certificate required

netcapture.title: API Capture
netcapture.subtitle: Observe a local app's API requests over CDP; pick one and turn it into a site descriptor for Auto Check-in. No certificate, no system proxy.
netcapture.exePathPh: Full path to the program you want to capture, e.g. C:\Program Files\App\App.exe
netcapture.probeNoTargets: The port answers but there is no capturable window yet (the app may not have opened its UI).
netcapture.probeRunningNoPort: The app is running, but it was started without a debug port. Chromium only accepts that flag at launch and cannot attach to a running process — close the app first, then use "Launch with debug port".
netcapture.launched: Started (debug port {port}); click "Probe port" once the app is up
netcapture.waitPort: Started. Wait for the app to come up, then click "Probe port" (port {port})
netcapture.needPath: Fill in the program path first
netcapture.idle: Not started. Set the debug port, then click "Probe port" to confirm the app is running with it.
netcapture.empty: Nothing captured yet. Start capturing, then perform the action in the target app (click the button you care about).
netcapture.copied: Copied — paste it into Auto Check-in's site descriptor
netcapture.copyFailed: Copy failed; select the text below and copy it manually
netcapture.saveFailed: Could not save the path; these settings will not persist
netcapture.rememberHint: Program path, port, env vars and filter are remembered — they will be here next time. Captured requests are not saved.
netcapture.presetRecognized: Recognized: {app}. Port and launch method are filled in for you — just click "Launch with debug port".
netcapture.envPlaceholder: One KEY=VALUE per line. Some apps ignore command-line flags and only read env vars — this is how you open their debug port.
netcapture.envHint: Some apps ignore command-line flags and only read environment variables — this is the second such app found in practice (Qoder's CDP_PORT, WorkBuddy's WORKBUDDY_REMOTE_DEBUGGING_PORT). If "launch" starts a process but the port never opens, this is why. Format: one KEY=VALUE per line, lines starting with # are ignored.
netcapture.editableHint: This box is editable. What you captured is just one request and is usually missing fields — especially the 'already checked in' field, which often lives in a different request. Edit it, then click add; the tool uses what you edited.
netcapture.markStatusTitle: Mark this as the "status" request. Some check-in endpoints contain an ID that changes daily, and that ID can only be read from the status response — so both must be selected.
netcapture.markStatusHint: If the check-in endpoint contains a daily-changing ID, also mark the status request (button on the right of each row) and generate from both.
netcapture.combineNote: Will be combined with status request {path}
netcapture.portReady: Started — debug port {port} is ready, you can start capturing
netcapture.portNeverOpened: The process started, but debug port {port} never opened. Common causes: this exe is only a launcher (it starts a background component, not the UI), or it is a Node SFA wrapper that rejects --remote-debugging-port as an invalid option and exits. Point this at the app's real executable, or start it with the flag yourself.
netcapture.launchNoPort: Started, but the debug port did not open — use "Probe port" to confirm
netcapture.siteExists: A site with the same key already exists and was NOT overwritten. Change the key or edit it in the check-in tool.
netcapture.addRejected: This request does not meet the check-in site requirements — see the errors below
netcapture.descriptorIncomplete: Generated, but some fields need you to fill in — see the notes below
netcapture.whyTitle: Why does the target app have to restart?
netcapture.why1: Chromium only accepts a debug port **at launch** and cannot attach to a running process. So the app you want to capture must be closed and restarted with the flag.
netcapture.why2: This uses CDP instead of installing a root certificate: no system proxy, no trusted CA, and only the one app is affected — not every HTTPS connection on the machine.
netcapture.why3: Chromium never hands cookies to the capture side at all, so credentials show up as redacted placeholders. The check-in tool needs them from the app itself — don't paste them into a chat; the tool encrypts them at rest.
